# Appeal of Denial – Total Hip Replacement (CPT 27130)

**Member:** Taylor Ellison
**Member ID:** W798611035
**Plan:** Independence Blue Cross (Commercial/ACA), Pennsylvania
**Denial date:** 2026-08-02
**Reference number:** POC-2FE0EDCD1B-73051
**Governing policy named in my denial:** Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines – Musculoskeletal: Joint Surgery (2025-11-15), https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/

Dear Independence Blue Cross Member Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my total hip replacement (CPT 27130), referenced above. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider its decision.

## Why I am appealing

The denial notice states that my records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I want to lay out what conservative care I actually completed, and I want to be transparent about the policy language available to me.

**A note on the policy criteria:** The excerpts I was given from the Carelon Musculoskeletal: Joint Surgery guideline address shoulder arthroplasty, hemiarthroplasty, and reverse shoulder arthroplasty — not hip replacement. I do not have the specific hip replacement section of this policy in front of me, so I am not able to quote the plan's exact hip-related criteria here. I am asking the plan to review my records against the actual hip replacement criteria in its own policy, and I am setting out below, in my own words, why I believe my conservative care history should meet whatever "adequate trial" standard applies.

## The conservative care I completed

- **Symptom duration:** I have had progressive hip pain for 18 months that has not been relieved by rest.
- **Physical therapy:** I completed 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy (2026-02-20 to 2026-06-12), totaling 16 visits, focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication:** I took NSAIDs for 4 months without adequate relief.
- **Injection:** I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-21, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging:** A weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph on 2026-06-13 showed joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes.
- **Function:** I now ambulate with a cane, am limited to walking one block, and cannot put on my own shoes without help.
- **Exam:** My physical exam showed positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- **No contraindications:** I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I do not smoke.

Given this history — 18 months of pain, 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy, 4 months of NSAID use, and a corticosteroid injection that gave only brief relief — I believe the record shows a genuine, documented trial of conservative management that did not resolve my symptoms, alongside radiographic evidence of advanced joint disease.

## What I am asking

I am asking Independence Blue Cross to reconsider this denial in light of the conservative care and imaging findings summarized above, and to evaluate my case against the specific hip replacement criteria in the Carelon Musculoskeletal: Joint Surgery guideline. If there are additional records that would help — such as the full physical therapy discharge note, imaging report, or a letter from Dr. Duval — I am prepared to provide them.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-01-29 (180 days from the date of this notice), and I am submitting it well within that window.

Please send your decision, and any further instructions, to the address or phone number below.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Taylor Ellison
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Date]

By phone: 1-888-671-5276

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
